answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by treating identity as a verifiable thread of completed work: every finished job is sealed by its counterparty into a tamper-evident record, so reputation is earned task by task, never claimed. A new identity starts with an empty thread and must build one slowly, while honest agents carry long cross-checked histories. Forging a hundred fakes means doing a hundred agents' worth of real paid work. Like grading an opal, verifiers inspect the thread's depth — a thin fresh record fails — and like ivory, a genuine history cannot be carved overnight.
